about.title: Walnut Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Walnut's mix of business parks, retail centers, and light industrial sites along Grand Avenue, Amar Road, Lemon Avenue, and La Puente Road means workers here face everyday risks — forklift accidents, delivery truck collisions, ladder falls, and equipment malfunctions among them. Most on-the-job injuries in California are handled through workers' compensation, but that system doesn't always cover everything a worker loses, and it usually can't be used to sue your own employer. When a subcontractor, property owner, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp case. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Walnut workers with an independent attorney who can look at the facts, explain your options, and help you understand whether a third-party claim applies to your situation. There's no cost to find out, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Walnut Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Blocked by Workers' Comp
items.desc: California generally limits your claim against your employer to workers' comp, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held responsible in a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early
items.desc: California workers generally have 30 days to report a jobsite injury to their employer, and missing that window can complicate both workers' comp and any related third-party case.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue a claim, so raising concerns about a jobsite incident is legally protected.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says it was my fault?
items.answer: Workers' compensation in California generally doesn't require proving fault, so an employer's opinion about how the injury happened usually doesn't block your claim. If a third party outside your employer contributed to the incident, fault may become more relevant to that separate claim. An independent attorney can review the specifics with you.

items.question: What if my injury happened near one of Walnut's busier roads, like Amar Road or Grand Avenue?
items.answer: If your job involves driving, deliveries, or working near traffic on corridors like Amar Road or Grand Avenue, a collision caused by another driver could support a third-party claim in addition to workers' comp. These cases often involve looking at who was actually at fault for the crash itself. An attorney can help sort out which claims apply.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim in California?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from the 30-day window for reporting an injury to your employer under workers' comp rules. Because these timelines run differently, it helps to get guidance sooner rather than later.
